title: In one lab study, 6- to 9-month-olds looked at named foods and body parts
summary: Bergelson and Swingley reported that 6- to 9-month-olds looked more at a food or body-part picture when a parent named it.
body: In a 2012 paper, Elika Bergelson and Daniel Swingley tested 33 infants from 6 to 9 months. Parents named pictures the infants had not been taught in the lab. On paired pictures, 26 of the 33 infants had a positive mean difference score, looking more toward the named picture, and the group result was statistically significant. The pictures were foods and body parts. The authors say the study does not establish the size of each infant's vocabulary or exactly which of the tested words each child knew. Scene pictures, with several items together, were a weaker test.

sources.title: At 6-9 months, human infants know the meanings of many common nouns
sources.author: Elika Bergelson and Daniel Swingley
sources.note: Opened 2026-11-26 at the PMC page. Peer-reviewed paper. Supports the paired-picture result, 26 of 33 infants, foods and body parts, and the authors' limit that vocabulary size is not established.
